title: Terminal starts while the Obsidian window is off screen
why: Upstream, startEmulator waits for Ne(el), a check that the plugin stylesheet applies. Ne sets display:none, adds the await-css class (its rule sets display:unset !important), and waits until an IntersectionObserver reports that the element is visible. The observer never fires for a window that is hidden, covered, or on another workspace. So a terminal that opens while Obsidian is not on screen does not start its shell until the window shows. Orbh launches from Strike often hit this, because Obsidian is behind the launching app. The edit keeps the purpose of the check but reads the result with getComputedStyle, which also works off screen. It uses the observer only when the class rule does not apply yet.
